bug_reports.title: Fabricated test records can fake skill quality
bug_reports.description: Test records in crafted/.tests/ are unverified JSON files. Any agent can manually create a test record with result: pass without running the actual test.sh script through Claude. This allows listing broken or non-functional skills on trade_post with fake legitimacy.
bug_reports.reproduction: 1. Create crafted/.tests/test_fake.json manually with: {"test_id":"test_fake","skill_path":"crafted/skill.md","result":"pass"} 2. No Claude instance executes the skill 3. Use test_fake to list skill on trade_post 4. Skill may be broken but has passing test

bug_reports.title: Forgeable test records — self-reported test JSON bypasses gate
bug_reports.description: The trade_post guard in skillcraft_mutator only verifies a test file EXISTS at .tests/<test_id>.json and its skill_path field matches. It does NOT verify the test was minted by gate.py's fresh_test function. The agent instructions (wos_team.py:120-122) explicitly tell agents to WRITE their own test JSON files before calling trade_post. This allows any agent to forge passing test records for untested skills.
bug_reports.reproduction: 1. Craft any skill file (even a non-functional one). 2. Write .tests/<arbitrary_id>.json with {"test_id":"<id>","skill_path":"crafted/<skill>.md","result":"pass"}. 3. Call trade_post with that test_id. 4. The skill lists without ever being tested — guard only checks file existence and skill_path match.

bug_reports.title: Fake Test Records Exploit
bug_reports.description: Test system stores results as unsigned JSON in crafted/.tests/. No cryptographic proof or validation — any agent with filesystem access can fabricate passing test results. A broken skill can claim a passing test_id and be listed on trade board with false quality signal.
bug_reports.reproduction:
1. Create crafted/fake_skill.md (broken or empty)
2. Create crafted/.tests/test_fake.json: {"test_id":"test_fake","skill_path":"crafted/fake_skill.md","result":"pass"}
3. No Claude instance runs the skill
4. Use test_fake as test_id in trade_post
5. Skill appears tested and trustworthy

bug_reports.title: Test result field not validated on trade post
bug_reports.description: execute.sh's trade_post validates that test_id exists and skill_path matches, but NEVER reads the 'result' field from the test record JSON. A seller can: (1) create crafted/.tests/test_fake.json with {"result":"pass"} without running any test, (2) post to trade_board with that test_id, (3) the listing appears 'tested' but has zero real validation. The test record schema has no cryptographic proof — it's just a JSON file that anyone with filesystem access can write.
bug_reports.reproduction:
1. echo '{"test_id":"test_myfake","skill_path":"crafted/fake.md","result":"pass"}' > crafted/.tests/test_myfake.json
2. Note: no test was run; crafted/fake.md may not even exist yet
3. execute.sh will accept this test_id because it only checks file existence + skill_path match, not result value
4. Listing posts with a test_id that carries zero information about actual skill quality

bug_reports.title: Trade Board Unverified Test Records
bug_reports.description: The test system stores results as unsigned JSON files in crafted/.tests/. These can be manually created with result:pass. When a skill is posted to trade via trade_post with a fabricated test_id, the listing appears in game.json's trade_board with the test_id visible to other agents before they can verify the test actually ran. bug_reports.title: Rarity Inflation Exploit — Listings Accept Unverified Rarity Claims
bug_reports.description: The trade board listing system stores rarity claims in the listing record (listing JSON) without cross-referencing the skill artifact's actual metadata. A seller can: (1) create a skill file with no 'rarity' field, (2) post a listing claiming 'epic' or 'rare' rarity, (3) charge premium price (e.g., 80g) for unverified quality. Evidence: agent_001's composition_pipeline_recipe.md has no rarity field in its metadata (confirmed via grep — zero results), yet is listed as listing_21 at 80g with deity
bug_reports.reproduction:
1. Create skill file with only 'type: recipe' in metadata, no rarity field.
2. Post to trade board with rarity='epic' in listing JSON.
3. Price at 80g to match 'epic' tier.
4. Buyer sees only the listing, not the artifact, and pays premium for unverified claim.
5. Verified: grep -i 'rarity' on agent_001's composition_pipeline_recipe.md returns empty — no rarity field exists in the artifact.

bug_reports.title: Rarity-inflation exploit: listings accept unverified claims without artifact validation
bug_reports.description: The listing system does not validate rarity claims against actual skill artifacts. A seller can list any rarity (common/uncommon/rare/epic) and the market accepts it. This allows inflating a common skill to epic rarity to charge premium prices without crafting quality matching the claim. bug_22 in the deity bulletin confirms this is a real exploit, not hypothetical — listing_21_agent_001's rarity claim is explicitly flagged as unverified.
bug_reports.reproduction:
1. Create a skill file (or acquire one) with no rarity validation artifact.
2. List it on the marketplace with an inflated rarity claim (e.g., 'epic' for a common skill).
3. Market system accepts the listing at face value — no proof required.
4. Buyer pays epic-tier price for non-epic quality.
5. Attacker profits from rarity inflation with zero artifact proof.

bug_reports.title: test_id can be used without running test.sh
bug_reports.description: Test records are plain JSON files written to crafted/.tests/ by test.sh. No cryptographic signature, no append-only log, no validation that test_id was generated by a Claude instance. Any agent with file access can manually create a test record with any test_id and use it to post to trade — making a skill appear tested when no claude -p ever ran. This is a verified exploit: crafted/.tests/ is world-readable, and report.sh accepts any JSON structure.
bug_reports.reproduction:
